header.title: Control Structures
header.subtitle: Foundation Level • 60 minutes • Master decision-making and repetition in Python

introduction.title: Introduction to Control Structures
introduction.paragraph1: Control structures are the backbone of programming logic. They allow you to control the flow of your program, make decisions based on conditions, and repeat actions efficiently.
introduction.callout: What you'll learn: Master if/elif/else statements for decision-making, for and while loops for repetition, loop control with break and continue, and how to combine these structures effectively.

conditional.title: Conditional
conditional.description: Make decisions with if, elif, and else statements

iterative.title: Iterative
iterative.description: Repeat actions with for and while loops

controlFlow.title: Control Flow
controlFlow.description: Modify loop behavior with break and continue

whyReasons: Enable programs to make intelligent decisions
Handle different scenarios and user inputs

ifStatements.title: If Statements
ifStatements.paragraph1: If statements allow your program to make decisions by executing different code blocks based on whether conditions are true or false.
operatorItems: or - At least one condition must be true
noteItems: Python uses indentation to define code blocks (usually 4 spaces)
The elif keyword is short for "else if"
The else clause is optional and catches all other cases

forLoops.title: For Loops
forLoops.paragraph1: For loops are used to iterate over sequences like lists, strings, or ranges. They're perfect when you know how many times you want to repeat something.

rangeStartStop.title: range(start, stop)
rangeStartStop.description: Generates numbers from start to stop-1

whileLoops.title: While Loops
whileLoops.paragraph1: While loops continue executing as long as a condition remains true. They're useful when you don't know exactly how many iterations you need.
infiniteLoopsItems: Always modify the condition variable inside the loop
Make sure the condition can eventually become false
bestPracticesItems: Keep the condition simple and clear
Update condition variables inside the loop
Consider using for loops when possible
whenToUseItems: Input validation (keep asking until valid input)
Menu systems (keep showing menu until user quits)
Waiting for certain conditions to be met
Game loops that run until game over

loopControl.title: Loop Control: Break and Continue
loopControl.paragraph1: Break and continue statements give you fine control over loop execution, allowing you to exit loops early or skip specific iterations.
breakItems: Works in both for and while loops
continueItems: Skips the rest of the current iteration
Useful for filtering or skipping items
Does not exit the loop completely
loopControl.breakUseCases: Search algorithms, input validation, early exit conditions
loopControl.continueUseCases: Data filtering, skipping invalid items, processing only certain elements

nestedStructures.title: Nested Control Structures
nestedStructures.paragraph1: You can combine control structures by nesting them inside each other. This allows for complex logic and multi-dimensional data processing.

exercise1.title: Exercise 1: Grade Calculator
exercise1.description: Create a program that assigns letter grades based on numeric scores using if-elif-else statements.

exercise2.title: Exercise 2: Number Patterns
exercise2.description: Use nested for loops to create number patterns and shapes.

exercise3.title: Exercise 3: Number Guessing Game
exercise3.description: Build a number guessing game using while loops and control statements.

exercise4.title: Exercise 4: Data Processing
exercise4.description: Process a list of numbers using loops and control statements.
